name: Kassite
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page kass1244 (Kassite, Unclassifiable, IQ)
sources.note: No references at all listed for this languoid.

sources.citation: Fournet, Arnaud. 2011. The Kassite language in a comparative perspective with Hurrian and Urartean. The Macro-Comparative Journal 2(1): 1-19.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Lexicon (ca. 60 words) and onomastic morphology compared with Hurrian; only phonological remark is a quotation of Purves (NPN 184) that 'the phonemic systems of the two [Hurrian and Kassite] languages seem to be largely alike' (p. 3).

sources.citation: Zadok, Ran. Kassites. Encyclopaedia Iranica online (2005/2012).
sources.note: Modern survey with a linguistic section and full bibliography.

sources.citation: Pinches, Theophilus G. 1917. The language of the Kassites. Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society 49(1): 101-114.
sources.note: Nothing. Cuneiform copy and transliteration of the 48-line Kassite-Babylonian vocabulary tablet plus an alphabetic word/name list; no phonology, no accent or stress (a full-text search for stress/accent the scanned text for accent/stress/pronunciation: no hits).

sources.citation: Delitzsch, Friedrich. 1884. Die Sprache der Kossäer: linguistisch-historische Funde und Fragen. Leipzig: J. C. Hinrichs. 94 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. II 'Die Sprache der Kossäer' (pp. 21-51) is a line-by-line commentary on the vocabulary tablet and on names; the only remark on sound structure is a conjecture (p. 38) that Kassite, like Sumerian, may have let a word-final consonant fade ('vocalischer Nominalauslaut'). No Betonung/Akzent anywhere in the scanned text.

Nothing on phonology; both state that a Kassite grammar cannot be reconstructed from the scant material (de: 'Eine kassitische Grammatik kann wegen der Dürftigkeit des Materials zurzeit nicht rekonstruiert werden'). Used only for their bibliographies.

sources.citation: Brinkman, J. A. 1976-80. Kassiten. Reallexikon der Assyriologie 5: 464-473.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Standard encyclopedia article with a section on the language; would confirm that grammar/phonology are unrecoverable.

sources.note: Lexical isoglosses with Hurro-Urartian; low chance of a stress remark.
